usage:
import os

from openai import Client

client = Client(
    api_key=os.environ.get("OPENAI_API_KEY"),
)

result = client.beta.threads.runs.steps.retrieve("thread_id", "run_id", "step_id", include=["step_details.tool_calls[*].file_search.results[*].content"])
print(result)

fields.name: include
fields.description:
A list of additional fields to include in the response. Currently the only supported value is `step_details.tool_calls[*].file_search.results[*].content` to fetch the file search result content.

See the [file search tool documentation](/docs/assistants/tools/file-search#customizing-file-search-settings) for more information.

fields.name: id
fields.description: The identifier of the run step, which can be referenced in API endpoints.

fields.name: object
fields.description: The object type, which is always `thread.run.step`.

fields.name: created_at
fields.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the run step was created.

fields.name: assistant_id
fields.description: The ID of the [assistant](/docs/api-reference/assistants) associated with the run step.

fields.name: thread_id
fields.description: The ID of the [thread](/docs/api-reference/threads) that was run.

fields.name: run_id
fields.description: The ID of the [run](/docs/api-reference/runs) that this run step is a part of.

fields.name: type
fields.description: The type of run step, which can be either `message_creation` or `tool_calls`.

fields.name: status
fields.description: The status of the run step, which can be either `in_progress`, `cancelled`, `failed`, `completed`, or `expired`.

fields.name: step_details
fields.description: The details of the run step.
